newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas still off late, Mar holds support.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas still off late, Mar holds support.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained mostly lower late Wednesday in sluggish trade, with expectations for only a modest weekly stock draw and more technical selling again driving March near key support.
At 1428 EST, March slipped 7.1 cents to $2.475 per million British thermal units, while April was 6.2 cents lower at $2.195. Most others were down by one to 3.7 cents.

"I think the market is slowly giving up on the bullish stock picture. There may be another few weeks of cold weather, but the market is feeling comfortable with stocks," said one Houston trader, adding he expected March to break support.

Traders said forecasts for colder Midwest and Northeast weather were offset by a comfortable inventory cushion in the East, and most agreed only colder temperatures in Texas and the South would reignite the bull market.

Withdrawal estimates for Wednesday's weekly AGA storage report averaged 140-155 bcf versus a 161 bcf decline for the same week last year. Traders said the eastern stock surplus of 173 bcf, or 19 percent, would make a sustained rally difficult.
But some technical traders disagreed, noting the market was extremely oversold and due for a bounce.
"The oversold stochastics could lead to a technical rally. There may be a little more life left in the bull, but I'm a little concerned," said a New York-based trader.
Technical traders saw key March support at the double bottom and recent low of $2.46, with next support in the $2.35 area. Resistance was seen at $2.70 and $2.80.

In the cash, February Gulf Coast prices were off five cents or more Wednesday to the mid-to-high $2.80s. Feb Midcon pipes also were off by about five cents to the mid-$2.70s. New York city gate gas for Feb delivery was quoted little changed in the $3.60s.
NYMEX said 17,473 Hub contracts traded by 1355 EST.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas were untraded at 1215 EST. February Alberta and Permian natgas expire today.
On the KCBT, March slipped 7.5 cents to $2.235, while deferreds were four to eight cents lower. The East/West spread widened by 0.4 cent to 24 cents (NYMEX premium).
